narrative.headline: Steering tops 2018 Jeep Wrangler complaints by a wide margin
narrative.summary: Owners filed 1,784 complaints to NHTSA. Steering dominates at 1,111 reports (62%) and is tied to 9 crashes and 3 injuries. Suspension is a distant second (342, 19%). Fire shows up most in the powertrain and engine reports, even though those categories are smaller. No deaths were reported in any category.

issues.title: Steering
issues.blurb: The single biggest concern by far: 1,111 reports (62% of all complaints), linked to 9 crashes and 3 injuries. Owners describe a sudden steering wobble at speed that makes the wheel hard to control. Test-drive at highway speed and have the steering and front-end checked before you buy.

issues.title: Suspension
issues.blurb: Second most reported at 342 reports (19%), tied to 1 crash and 3 injuries. No fires reported here. Watch for handling that feels loose or unstable at highway speed during a test drive.

issues.title: Electrical System
issues.blurb: 254 reports (14%), with 5 fires, 2 crashes, and 1 injury. Confirm all warning lights work and clear, and that the vehicle holds power normally on a test drive.

issues.title: Power Train
issues.blurb: Smaller in volume (168 reports, 9%) but the highest fire count of any category at 13 fires, plus 2 crashes and 2 injuries. Owners report the vehicle shutting down with transmission and engine warnings. A pre-purchase inspection is worth it here.

issues.title: Engine
issues.blurb: Fewest reports here (96, 5%), but they skew serious: 7 fires, 3 crashes, and 2 injuries. Have a mechanic inspect the engine bay for any signs of overheating or fire risk before buying.
